What the official sources say

  • The board fixes property at 60 percent of true and actual value if assessed above or below that, and no assessment may exceed 60 percent of true and actual value. (W. Va. Code §11-3-24; source)
  • An assessment may not be increased without at least five days' written notice to the taxpayer. (W. Va. Code §11-3-24; source)
  • A person who fails to apply for relief at the board meeting waives the right to seek correction for the current year except on appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals or as otherwise provided. (W. Va. Code §11-3-24; source)
  • An Office of Tax Appeals petition from a valuation or a Board of Equalization and Review order must be filed by March 31 of the property tax year or it is dismissed as untimely. (W. Va. Code §11-3-25b; source)
  • The former circuit-court relief section for erroneous assessments, §11-3-25, is marked repealed. (W. Va. Code §11-3-25; source)
  • West Virginia sells tax liens at public auction; unsold tracts may be sold by the Auditor without further advertising or auction. (W. Va. Code §11A-3-2; source)

How does West Virginia property tax work from assessment to bill?

Each property is assessed once a year as of July 1 at sixty percent of its true and actual value, a county levy rate is applied the following calendar year, and the sheriff mails the bill and collects it in two installments. W. Va. Code 11-3-1 defines the assessment date as July 1 of the year before the tax year, and the tax year as the next calendar year that begins after that date.

For an owner selling a house, the calendar is the useful part. A July 1 value drives the next year's bill, a bill is issued in summer, and the first half falls due early in September. Closing in the middle of that cycle means the seller and buyer have to sort out who pays what.

  • Assessor: values real and personal property and keeps the records.
  • County commission: sits as the board of equalization and review each February.
  • Levying bodies: the state, county commission, school board and any municipality set the rates, within limits.
  • Sheriff: sends the tax ticket and collects payment.

What does "true and actual value" mean for a home?

It is the price the property would sell for if voluntarily offered by the owner on the terms such property usually sells, and not the price at a forced sale (W. Va. Code 11-3-1(a)). For owner-occupied residential property, the statute also tells the assessor to consider the fair and reasonable income the property might earn if rented, under normal conditions in the locality.

The Tax Commissioner's biennial report adds that each assessor must keep values current by having a staff member visit each parcel of real property in repeating three-year cycles to check for changes. The report states the sixty percent rule plainly: assessed value must be 60 percent of the property's true and actual value.

A worked example, for illustration only: a home with a true and actual value of $150,000 would have an assessed value of $90,000. The tax is the rate times that assessed value.

What are the property classes and maximum rates?

West Virginia sorts property into four classes, and the class decides the maximum rate. The Tax Commissioner's report defines them this way.

  • Class I: tangible personal property used exclusively in agriculture, farm products held by the producer, and intangible personal property.
  • Class II: property owned, used and occupied by the owner exclusively for residential purposes, and farms occupied and cultivated by their owners or bona fide tenants.
  • Class III: all other real and personal property outside municipalities.
  • Class IV: all other real and personal property inside municipalities.
Taxing authorityClass IClass IIClass IIIClass IV
State0.25 cents0.50 cents1.00 cent1.00 cent
County14.3028.6057.2057.20
Schools22.9545.9091.8091.80
Municipal12.5025.00not applicable50.00
Total maximum50.00100.00150.00200.00

The figures are maximum regular levy rates in cents per $100 of assessed value, from the Tax Commissioner's 55th biennial report covering fiscal years 2019 to 2023. Voters of a county, school board or municipality can approve excess levies above those maximums, but the state itself cannot exceed its rate. The report also says statewide the average rate for all property was $1.90 per $100 of assessed valuation. Your actual rate depends on your levy district and any excess levies, so check the sheriff's ticket for the real number.

When are West Virginia property taxes due?

Taxes are payable in two installments: the first is due September 1 of the tax year and becomes delinquent on October 1, and the second is due March 1 and becomes delinquent April 1 (W. Va. Code 11A-1-3(a)). The Tax Division's due-date page confirms the same dates.

ItemDate or rate
Assessment dateJuly 1 of the year before the tax year
Tax tickets issued by sheriffsOn or after July 15 of the tax year
Public utility bills (State Auditor)June of the tax year
First half due; delinquentSeptember 1; October 1
Second half due; delinquentMarch 1; April 1
Discount for paying by the due date2.5 percent
Interest on delinquent taxes9 percent per year

Taxes paid on or before the date they are payable get the two and one-half percent discount, and interest at nine percent per annum is added from the delinquency date until paid. The sheriff must mail each taxpayer a ticket to the last known address by first-class mail, but section 11A-1-8 says failure of the sheriff to send it, or of the taxpayer to receive it, does not impair the right to collect the tax, interest or penalty. If you sold or bought a house recently, make sure the ticket goes to the right address.

Is there a homestead exemption in West Virginia?

Yes, for older and disabled owners. W. Va. Code 11-6B-3 exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of a homestead that the owner uses and occupies exclusively for residential purposes, when the owner is 65 or older or certified as permanently and totally disabled.

  • The owner must have been or will be a West Virginia resident for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year concerned, with limited exceptions for people who left and returned and for certain military service members.
  • An owner who receives a similar exemption in another state is not eligible, and the application includes a sworn affidavit on that point.
  • Only one exemption is allowed per homestead, however many qualified owners live there.
  • The exemption attaches to the homestead occupied on the July 1 assessment date and applies to the next tax year.

For sellers this has a direct effect. If a qualified owner's homestead is transferred by deed, will or otherwise, the $20,000 exemption is removed on the next July 1 assessment date unless the new owner qualifies. A buyer should not assume the seller's lower bill will continue. Under section 11-6B-4, an owner 65 or older who has filed once with the assessor does not need to refile unless moving to a new homestead.

How do I appeal a West Virginia property assessment?

Start with the assessor, then the county commission sitting as the board of equalization and review in February. Section 11-3-24 requires the commission to meet by February 1 of the tax year, allows it to adjourn after February 15 and requires it to adjourn by the last day of February.

The board reviews and corrects valuation, but it may not consider questions of classification or taxability. If you question a classification, section 11-3-24a lets a taxpayer ask the assessor for information and protest, with a path to the Tax Commissioner and the Office of Tax Appeals. The board can fix any assessment found above or below sixty percent at sixty percent, and no assessment can be increased without at least five days' written notice.

A person who fails to apply for relief at the board meeting waives the right to ask for correction of the current year's list, except by appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals or as otherwise provided. A taxpayer who elects a hearing may appeal the board's order to that office. Section 11-3-23a also describes an informal review in which a taxpayer may apply for relief to the board or the Office of Tax Appeals by February 20 of the tax year with a written protest.

Because the deadlines are tight and a missed February meeting can cost a year, mark them on a calendar early.

What taxes and fees apply when a West Virginia house is sold?

The main transfer charge is the real property transfer tax on the deed: $1.10 for each $500 of value or fraction, plus a $20 fee for transferring real estate for consideration (W. Va. Code 11-22-2). The county clerk collects both when recording. Under the same section, starting July 1, 2025, the excise tax is a county tax retained by the county where it was collected.

The clerk handles recording at the county courthouse, and the sheriff handles property tax. At a closing, ask the closing agent or title company to request a current tax statement from the sheriff, confirm which installments are paid, and see that unpaid ones are settled from proceeds.

Sellers with back taxes should read the Tax Division's due-date page and ask the county sheriff for a payoff figure before choosing a buyer. A cash sale to us as-is can include a house with tax due, and we can walk through the numbers with you. We do not promise a price here, and the amount depends on the house and the payoff.

More questions about West Virginia Property Tax Guide

What is the West Virginia property tax assessment ratio?

Sixty percent. Property is assessed annually as of July 1 at sixty percent of its true and actual value (W. Va. Code 11-3-1(a)). The tax rate is applied to that assessed value.

When is the first half of West Virginia property tax due?

September 1 of the tax year. It becomes delinquent on October 1. The second half is due March 1 and becomes delinquent April 1 (W. Va. Code 11A-1-3). A 2.5 percent discount applies to payments made by the due dates.

What interest applies to late West Virginia property tax?

Nine percent per year. Interest at nine percent per annum is added from the date the tax becomes delinquent until paid, for both the first and second installments.

Who qualifies for the West Virginia homestead exemption?

Owners age 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, who own and live in the home. The exemption covers the first $20,000 of assessed value and requires two consecutive calendar years of state residency before the tax year, with exceptions in section 11-6B-3.

What is the West Virginia real property transfer tax?

$1.10 for each $500 of value or fraction, plus a $20 fee for transferring real estate for consideration, collected by the county clerk when the deed is recorded (W. Va. Code 11-22-2).

Can I sell a West Virginia house with property tax still owed?

Yes. The owed amount is normally settled from the sale proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the county sheriff first, and tell any buyer, including us, about the balance up front.

West Virginia Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Cash Home Buyers in West Virginia

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a West Virginia Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the West Virginia Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a West Virginia House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • A claimant aged 65 or older need not refile after the first claim unless moving to a new homestead. (W. Va. Code §11-6B-4; source)
Selling in West Virginia?
We buy West Virginia houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Who qualifies for the West Virginia homestead exemption?

An owner qualifies if the home is their exclusive residence and they are 65 or older or certified permanently and totally disabled. Section 11-6B-3 of the West Virginia Code exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of a homestead that the owner uses and occupies exclusively for residential purposes.

The West Virginia Tax Division lists the exemption among its property tax exemptions and words it the same way: owner-occupied residential property owned by a person 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.

The program has no income test in the statute we read. It also allows only one exemption for each homestead, no matter how many qualified owners live there.

RequirementWhat the statute says
AmountFirst $20,000 of assessed value
Owner65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled
UseUsed and occupied by the owner exclusively for residential purposes
ResidencyWest Virginia resident for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year
Other statesNo similar exemption in another state; sworn affidavit with the application
LimitOne exemption per homestead

What are the residency rules and the exceptions?

The owner must have been, or will be, a West Virginia resident for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year. The statute accepts a voter registration card or a motor vehicle registration card issued in West Virginia as proof, among other documents.

There are two exceptions. First, someone who left West Virginia and came back within five years can qualify without the two consecutive years, as long as they were a resident for two calendar years out of the ten calendar years before the tax year. Second, a person who was a West Virginia resident when entering active military duty, kept the state as their residence through service, and returned to the state and bought a homestead after retiring or separating because of a permanent and total disability is treated as meeting the residency test.

The statute also says an owner who receives a similar exemption for a homestead in another state is ineligible. That is why the application comes with the sworn affidavit. Anyone who splits time between West Virginia and another state should read this requirement closely before filing.

How do you file, and what is the deadline?

The claim goes to the assessor of the county where the home sits, and it must be filed on or before December 1 after the July 1 assessment date. Section 11-6B-4 sets that deadline. If the claimant is sick, away or otherwise disabled, the claim can be filed by a duly authorized agent.

The Tax Division's property tax page lists a county assessors directory covering all 55 counties, with office locations, phone numbers and website links. Each assessor handles the paperwork locally.

  • File with the assessor in the county where the homestead is located.
  • Meet the December 1 deadline after the July 1 assessment date.
  • Include the sworn affidavit that no similar exemption is claimed in another state.
  • For a disability claim, include one of the documents the statute lists.

Missing the date has a clear cost. Under section 11-6B-4, a person who does not file on or before December 1 is determined to have waived the exemption for the next tax year.

What proof of disability does West Virginia accept?

A disability claim must include one of eight kinds of documentation, and the statute's list is broad. The accepted items include a written certification from a West Virginia licensed medical or osteopathic doctor that the claimant is permanently and totally disabled, and a Social Security Administration certification that the claimant currently receives permanent and total disability benefits.

Other items on the list are a copy of the original Social Security award letter with a voided copy of a current benefit check, a current Medicare card with a voided benefit check, and a written certification from the Veterans Administration of total and permanent disability. Workers' compensation documentation and pneumoconiosis documentation certifying total and permanent disability also count, and the eighth item is any other lawfully recognized documentation.

A disabled claimant who has filed once does not have to refile each year, but must sign a statement agreeing to notify the assessor if they are no longer eligible. If the claim relied on benefits, the claimant must tell the assessor within thirty days after the benefits stop.

Do you have to reapply every year?

No. A claimant 65 or older who has filed once does not need to refile unless they move to a new homestead. Section 11-6B-4 says so directly, and a disabled claimant has a similar rule with the added notice duty described above.

The statute carves out one situation that would otherwise look like a move. An otherwise qualified claimant who lives with a family member, or in a nursing home, personal care home, rehabilitation center or similar facility because of illness, accident or infirmity is not treated as having moved to a new homestead. That matters for families who are deciding whether a parent's house should be sold while the parent is in care.

The exemption also attaches to the home the qualified owner occupies on the July 1 assessment date and applies to taxes for the following tax year. It does not travel with the owner. Section 11-6B-3 says it cannot be transferred to another homestead until the following July 1.

What happens to the exemption when the house is sold or inherited?

When the home is transferred by deed, will or otherwise, the $20,000 exemption is removed on the next July 1 assessment date unless the new owner qualifies. A buyer who is under 65 and not disabled will not get it, so the property tax bill on the same house can rise after a sale.

For sellers, the practical effects are modest but real. The property tax ticket for the current year is still due on the schedule in section 11A-1-3: first installment payable September 1 and delinquent October 1, second installment payable March 1 and delinquent April 1. A two and one-half percent discount applies to payments made by the payable dates, and nine percent annual interest accrues on delinquent amounts. The county sheriff issues the tickets on or after July 15, according to the Tax Division.

Heirs face the same removal rule when a parent who held the exemption dies. If an heir keeps the house and qualifies in their own right, they can file their own claim by December 1. If the heirs sell, the exemption stops mattering to them once the deed is recorded. Our estate and inheritance tax guide covers the other costs on an inherited house.

How does the exemption fit with how West Virginia assesses homes?

West Virginia assesses property at 60 percent of fair market value, and the exemption comes off that assessed figure. A Tax Division summary states that the Constitution specifies assessed value as 60 percent of fair market value. Arithmetic shows a $20,000 assessed exemption therefore covers about $33,333 of market value, though the actual savings depend on the local levy rates, which we do not quote here.

The Tax Division says property taxes are levied by county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State. It also explains that the Constitution divides property into four classes, and Class II is owner-occupied residential property used exclusively for residential purposes. A home that qualifies as Class II is the kind of property the homestead exemption is written for.

If you disagree with an assessed value, the protest goes to the county commission sitting as a board of equalization and review. That board starts meeting February 1 each year, may adjourn any time after February 15 if its work is done, and must adjourn no later than February 28.

  • Assessment date: July 1 each year.
  • Exemption claim deadline: December 1.
  • Protest window: the county board meets starting February 1.
  • Tickets: issued on or after July 15.

What if you want to sell the house instead of keeping it?

The exemption ends with ownership. If you are 65 or older, behind on repairs and wondering whether to stay, the property tax saving is one number to weigh against upkeep costs.

We buy houses in West Virginia as-is, with no commission and no repair requests. If you are considering a sale, tell us about the property and any tax notices you have received, and we can explain what a cash closing involves. Turning an offer down costs nothing.

More questions about West Virginia Homestead Exemption

How much is the West Virginia homestead exemption?

It exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner-occupied home. Because West Virginia assesses at 60 percent of fair market value, that amount of assessed value corresponds to about $33,333 of market value. The tax dollars saved depend on your local levy rates.

What age do you have to be to claim it?

You must be 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, and the home must be your exclusive residence. Ask your county assessor how they apply the age date to your situation.

When is the filing deadline?

December 1, following the July 1 assessment date. The claim is filed with the assessor of the county where the home is located. A person who misses the date is treated as having waived the exemption for the next tax year.

Do I have to file every year?

No, if you are 65 or older and have filed once, you do not need to refile unless you move to a new homestead. Disabled claimants also need not refile, but must notify the assessor if they stop being eligible, within thirty days if benefits end.

Does the exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. If the home is transferred by deed, will or otherwise, the $20,000 exemption is removed on the next July 1 assessment date unless the new owner qualifies on their own. A buyer who is under 65 and not disabled will not qualify.

Can I get the exemption if I also claim one in another state?

No. An owner who receives a similar exemption for a homestead in another state is ineligible, and the application must come with a sworn affidavit that the owner is not receiving a similar exemption elsewhere.

title: West Virginia Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
West Virginia Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in West Virginia
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • West Virginia Estate and Inheritance Tax: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a West Virginia Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the West Virginia Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a West Virginia House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Section 11-11-3 imposes a West Virginia estate tax equal to the federal credit for state death taxes attributable to West Virginia property, whenever a federal estate tax is payable. (W. Va. Code §11-11-3; source)
Selling in West Virginia?
We buy West Virginia houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does West Virginia charge an estate or inheritance tax on a house?

West Virginia's estate tax statute only applies when a federal estate tax is payable, so most families selling an inherited house will not owe it. Section 11-11-3 of the West Virginia Code imposes the tax equal to the part of the federal credit for state death taxes that is attributable to West Virginia property, and it opens with the words "whenever a federal estate tax is payable to the United States."

That opening condition matters. For people who died in 2026, the IRS instructions for Form 706 say a federal estate tax return must be filed when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific exemption, is more than $15,000,000. An estate well under that figure has no federal estate tax payable, which means the state statute has nothing to attach to.

The statute also contains a fine-print floor. Section 11-11-2 defines the "federal credit" and says it may never be less than the credit that existed under older versions of the federal code. The IRS form instructions now refer to the "repeal of section 2011," the old credit section, and give a state death tax deduction on the return instead. How those two rules interact for a very large estate is a question for a probate attorney or the Tax Commissioner, and we do not try to answer it here.

What are the West Virginia estate tax filing rules if an estate is large enough?

If a West Virginia estate is subject to the tax, the personal representative files a return with the Tax Commissioner within nine months of the date of death. Section 11-11-8 sets that deadline, says the return goes to the Tax Commissioner's office in Charleston, and requires an executed copy of the federal estate tax return to be filed with it.

The same section says no West Virginia estate tax return needs to be filed if the estate is not subject to the tax. A beneficiary can also be asked to file. Once the Tax Commissioner sends notice, a beneficiary or anyone holding a legal or beneficial interest in the estate must provide the information requested about that interest.

ItemWhat the source saysSource
Trigger for the state taxA federal estate tax is payableW. Va. Code 11-11-3
State return dueWithin nine months after deathW. Va. Code 11-11-8(d)
Where filedTax Commissioner, CharlestonW. Va. Code 11-11-8(e)
Federal filing level, deaths in 2026More than $15,000,000 (gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption)IRS Form 706 instructions
Federal return timingGenerally nine months after death, with a six-month extension if requested before the due dateIRS filing page

The IRS describes the federal timing on its estate and gift tax returns page.

What is the nonprobate inventory and why does it matter when selling?

The nonprobate inventory is a sworn list of property that passes outside the will, and the personal representative must file it within 90 days of qualifying. Section 11-11-7 requires the personal representative to list and appraise, at fair market value on the date of death, all tangible and intangible nonprobate personal property the decedent owned or had an interest in.

The statute defines nonprobate personal property as property that does not pass by the will or by intestate descent and is not otherwise subject to administration in the estate. The form is filed with the clerk of the county commission or the fiduciary supervisor, together with the appraisement form required under chapter 44.

A house is real property, so it is not what this inventory lists. The same personal representative who files the inventory is usually the person who signs the sale paperwork.

  • Values are set as of the date of death.
  • The 90-day window runs from qualification of the personal representative.

What tax will heirs pay when they sell an inherited West Virginia house?

Heirs generally owe federal income tax only on any gain above their basis, and the basis of an inherited house is usually its fair market value on the date of death. The IRS explains on its gifts and inheritances page that basis for property inherited from a decedent is generally the fair market value on the date of death, or on the alternate valuation date if the executor files Form 706 and elects it.

If the house sells for more than that basis, the difference is a taxable gain. A date-of-death appraisal is worth getting early, even when no estate tax return is required, because it fixes the starting number.

The IRS adds two cautions. A 2015 law requires some recipients to use a basis consistent with the value finally reported on an estate tax return, and a recipient who receives a Schedule A to Form 8971 from an executor may need to report that consistent basis. An accuracy-related penalty can apply if someone uses a basis higher than the final estate tax value.

What closing costs and taxes come with the deed transfer in West Virginia?

West Virginia charges a transfer tax of $1.10 for each $500 of value, payable when the deed is presented for recording. Section 11-22-2 puts the tax on every person who delivers, accepts or presents a document for recording, and says it is payable at that moment.

The statute also describes who pays. Only one state tax and one county tax is paid on any one document, collected in the county where the document is first admitted to record, and the grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the document without the tax having been paid. For a transfer by a trustee, or a county clerk transferring land sold for taxes, the grantee pays.

A second, additional county excise tax exists too. It started in 1968 at 55 cents per $500, and the statute lets a county raise it to match the state rate, or to as much as $1.65 per $500 after July 1, 2017. The statute also says that from July 1, 2025 the first tax is a county excise tax retained by the county where it was collected. Exact county rates vary, so ask the county clerk where the deed will be recorded.

  • Rate under subsection (a): $1.10 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500.
  • Additional county tax under subsection (b): 55 cents per $500, with the county option to increase.
  • Payment: at delivery, acceptance or recording of the deed.

How do property taxes and the homestead exemption affect an inherited house?

Property tax keeps running while the estate is open, and the bills come from the county sheriff. The West Virginia Tax Division says ownership, use and value are set as of July 1 each year for the next calendar tax year, and that tickets are issued on or after July 15.

Under section 11A-1-3, taxes can be paid in two installments. The first is payable September 1 and delinquent October 1. The second is payable March 1 and delinquent April 1. Payment by the payable date earns a discount of two and one-half percent, and unpaid amounts carry nine percent annual interest from the delinquency date.

Inheriting a house can also change the bill. If the decedent was 65 or older and had the $20,000 homestead exemption, section 11-6B-3 says a transfer by deed, will or otherwise removes it on the next July 1 assessment date unless the new owner qualifies. An heir who moves in and is 65 or older, or is certified permanently and totally disabled, may qualify on their own. Our homestead exemption guide covers that filing.

A Tax Division summary adds that the Constitution sets assessed value at 60 percent of fair market value.

How does a cash sale work for heirs who want to close quickly?

A cash sale lets heirs sell the house as it stands, without repairs, showings or a buyer's loan approval. The personal representative signs the contract and deed, the title company checks liens and the estate's authority, and the transfer tax is paid at recording.

  • Confirm who is the qualified personal representative before signing anything.
  • Get a date-of-death value in writing, since it sets the heirs' basis.
  • Check that tax ticket installments are current at closing.
  • Ask the county clerk what the transfer tax will be on the deed.

We do not promise a price or timeline here. The call and text number is at the top of the page, and turning an offer down costs you nothing.

More questions about West Virginia Estate and Inheritance Tax

Does West Virginia have an inheritance tax?

The sources we reviewed describe an estate tax, not a separate inheritance tax on beneficiaries. Chapter 11, article 11 of the West Virginia Code is titled Estate Taxes, and section 11-11-3 imposes the tax only when a federal estate tax is payable. Ask a probate attorney or the Tax Commissioner about a large or unusual estate.

What is the federal estate tax filing level for 2026?

For people who died in 2026, the IRS instructions say Form 706 must be filed when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific exemption is more than $15,000,000. Below that figure no federal estate tax return is required for that reason.

When is a West Virginia estate tax return due?

Within nine months after the date of death, if the estate is subject to the tax. Section 11-11-8 says the return is filed with the Tax Commissioner in Charleston along with a copy of the federal estate tax return. No return is needed if the estate is not subject to the tax.

Do heirs pay capital gains tax when they sell an inherited house?

Only on gain above their basis. The IRS says basis for inherited property is generally the fair market value on the date of death, so a house sold soon afterward for about that value usually produces little or no gain. Keep the date-of-death appraisal with your tax records.

Who pays the West Virginia transfer tax on a deed?

The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without the tax paid. Section 11-22-2 sets the state-level rate at $1.10 per $500 of value, and a county can also levy an additional tax. For a transfer by a trustee, or a clerk's transfer of land sold for taxes, the grantee pays.

What happens to the homestead exemption when an heir takes the house?

It is removed on the next July 1 assessment date unless the new owner qualifies. Section 11-6B-3 allows the exemption only for an owner 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, who lives in the home. A claim must be filed with the county assessor by December 1.
